headline: BEARISH
headline_tag: Bitcoin stuck near $60,000 after a month of losses

action.title: CUT / defend tightly with a stop-loss
action.detail: Keep acquisition running but defend it tightly: the headline is BEARISH, Bitcoin is about 23% lower than a month ago and stuck around $60,000, fear is at 10 out of 100, and a Fed rate rise on 8 December is widely expected. No Rally watch window is open, so there is no rally to chase and no fresh drop alarm either. Put every acquisition campaign on a 30-day return stop-loss and pause the ones that miss it, trim spend aimed at active traders (they tend to leave before conditions improve), and move messaging toward stablecoins, safety and education. Keep a reserve rather than cutting to zero; step acquisition back up only once price closes above the 200-week average ($68,351) and then the 200-day average ($71,712). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: Down about 23% over 30 days; Bitcoin is stuck near $60,000.
Price is about 19% under its 50-day average, 38 days in a row.
The Fed meets on 8 December, with a rate rise widely expected.
watch: Fear is extreme, yet many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, so another slip could force those bets closed and make a drop sharper. A close above $62,250 and then $68,351 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the fall is easing; a close below $58,799 (the 30-day low) would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: the headline stays BEARISH and confidence has slipped to LOW; Bitcoin is stuck around $60,000, so today still calls for calm, safety-first messages and careful spending, not promotions. Short term, the mood is very fearful: Fear & Greed reads 10 out of 100, and Bitcoin, near $60,149, has closed under its 50-day average for 38 days in a row, about 19% below it. Even so, many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which could make any further slip sharper. A normal week lately swings about $4,069, so a close above $62,250 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $58,799 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; explainer and safety content fits better than offers.

The next month leans clearly down: price is about 23% lower than 30 days ago and about 23% lower than 90 days ago. The Fed meets on 8 December, and earlier this week markets put the chance of a rate rise there at about 98% (CME FedWatch via PANews); on the news side, Malaysia approved its first spot Bitcoin fund, listing on 2 December, while Argentina's central bank is reportedly leaning on platforms to curb stablecoin trading (both PANews). Bitcoin would have to win back $73,807 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. Keep bigger campaign pushes until after the Fed meeting and a clear turn.

Long term, the picture is flat rather than down: the 200-day average is still rising (about 3% over 90 days), but price is about 16% under it, about 12% under its 200-week average and about 52% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track while Bitcoin closes above $71,712 (the 200-day average); $68,351 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Banks keep opening doors, with Russia's VTB starting Bitcoin trading for qualified clients and Brazil's stock exchange and six large banks planning a real-backed stablecoin (both via PANews), but more weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and make keeping existing users the main use of budget.
